## Data wrangling
```{r, message=FALSE}
# Read three csv files into R
covar  <- read.csv("GSE85307_covar-1.csv")
expr   <- read.csv("GSE85307_geneExpression.csv")
linker <- read.csv("GSE85307_geneNames.csv")

# Rename the blank column header in gene expression file as "PROBEID" to match the 
#gene names file
names(expr)[1] <- "PROBEID"

# Check how many rows
nrow(expr)

# Merge the gene expression file with the linker file
expr_named <- merge(expr, linker, by = "PROBEID")

# Check to see if the number of rows is matching (=500)
nrow(expr_named)

# Convert the new expr_named into a long data
library(tidyverse)
longexprData <- expr_named %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("GSM"),
                      names_to = 'geoID',
                      values_to = 'Expression')

# Merge the long data with covariate data set matching geoID
df <- merge(longexprData, covar, by= "geoID")

sum(is.na(df$Expression))     # should be 0
length(unique(df$geoID))      # should be 157
nrow(df)                      # should be 500 * 157 = 78500

# Spot check that expression values stayed matched to the correct sample
#(a value in the merged data should equal the same cell in the original file)
s <- colnames(expr)[2]        # first sample column
df$Expression[df$PROBEID == 7924712 & df$geoID == s] ==
  expr[expr$PROBEID == 7924712, s]   # TRUE= it matches

# Look at the first 10 rows of df (specify to variables of interest)
head(df[, c("geoID", "GENE", "Expression", "preg_preeclampsia")], 10)
```

## Gene of interest and Variables of interest

(Identify one gene, one continuous covariate, and two categorical covariates of 
interest. At least one categorical variable should be derived from a continuous 
variable)

**Gene:** LIN9 (PROBEID 7924712). LIN9 was selected because it is measured in 
all 157 subjects and varies across them.

**Continuous covariate:** Maternal BMI ("mat_BMI", kg/m²). 

**Two categorical covariates:** 

1. Pregnancy outcome ("preg_preeclampsia"): Preeclampsia vs. Normal.
2. Vitamin D status ("vitD_status"): derived from the continuous variable 
maternal vitamin D ("mat_vitD", ng/mL) using the cutoffs <30 = Insufficient 
and >=30 = Sufficient. (Mirzakhani H, Litonjua AA, McElrath TF, et al. 
Early pregnancy vitamin D status and risk of preeclampsia. J Clin Invest. 
2016;126(12):4702-4715. doi:10.1172/JCI89031)
```{r}
# Remove the text prefix in chosen covariates and change BMI and vit D to numeric
df$mat_BMI  <- as.numeric(sub(".*: ", "", df$mat_BMI))
df$mat_vitD <- as.numeric(sub(".*: ", "", df$mat_vitD))
df$preg_preeclampsia <- sub(".*: ", "", df$preg_preeclampsia)

# Assign cut offs to vit D status from the continuous variable 
df$vitD_status <- ifelse(df$mat_vitD < 30, "Insufficient (<30 ng/mL)",
                         "Sufficient (>=30 ng/mL)")
# Filter to the chosen LIN9 gene 
geneData <- df %>% filter(GENE == "LIN9")
# Check the rows (should be 157)
nrow(geneData)
# Check group size and combinations 
table(geneData$vitD_status, useNA = "ifany") 
table(geneData$preg_preeclampsia, geneData$vitD_status) #Match the paper results
```
Finding two additional continuous variables, beside maternal BMI:

1. *Maternal age* (mat_age_yrs), which is a common covariate that would appear in
a Table 1. 

2. *Gestational age at delivery* (delivery_gestAge_wks), which is relevant to 
preeclampsia (often leads to earlier delivery)

```{r}
# Clean the extra prefix in the maternal age variable
df$mat_age_yrs <- sub(".*:","", df$mat_age_yrs)
# Check what type of variable is this
str(df$mat_age_yrs)
# Convert to numeric
df$mat_age_yrs <- as.numeric(df$mat_age_yrs)
# Check if it is numeric now
str(df$mat_age_yrs)

# Repeat the same with gestational age at delivery
df$delivery_gestAge_wks <- sub(".*:","", df$delivery_gestAge_wks)
str(df$delivery_gestAge_wks)
# Convert to numeric
df$delivery_gestAge_wks <- as.numeric(df$delivery_gestAge_wks)
str(df$delivery_gestAge_wks)

# Create the data that is filtered to one gene again so it includes the new 
#cleaned covariates, because otherwise the old geneData still have the two 
#covariates as characters
geneData <- df %>% filter(GENE == "LIN9")

# Use the filtered data (geneData) to check if the new covariates have any NAs
colSums(is.na(geneData[, c("mat_age_yrs", "delivery_gestAge_wks")])) # all 0 :)

```


Define a custom theme that will be applied to the three plots
```{r}
# Install ggtext to italicize text later
#install.packages("ggtext")
# Load ggtext 
library(ggtext)
# Define a custom theme
Theme <- theme(# Remove all the extra borders and grid lines
        panel.border = element_blank(), panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), 
        # Define the axis
        axis.line = element_line(colour = "black", linewidth = rel(1)),
        # element_markdown instead of element_text allow to use *...* to make
        #text italic (which will be used for gene names)
        axis.title.x = element_markdown(color = "black", face = 'bold', size=14),
        axis.title.y = element_markdown(color = "black", face = 'bold', size=14),
        axis.text  = element_markdown(color = "black", face='bold', size=14),
        # Set plot background
        plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
        panel.background = element_blank(),
        # Set the legend
        legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
        legend.text= element_markdown(color= "black", face='bold', size=13),
        legend.title= element_markdown(color= "black", face='bold', size=13),
        # Move legend to the top
        legend.position = 'top',
        # Set the plot title color and make it centered 
        plot.title = element_markdown(color = "black", 
                                  face = "bold", size = 15, hjust = 0.5))

```

## Generate a boxplot of Gene Expression separated by both categorical variables

The jitter function is learned by watching this youtube video:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mbvU8fF4eGM&t=9s

```{r}
# Compute a box plot using ggplot and the custom theme
p3 <- ggplot(geneData, aes(x = preg_preeclampsia, y = Expression, fill = vitD_status)) +
  # Add boxplot (hide outlier dots because every subject is plotted below -- this 
  #was pointed out by Claude when checking my plot with it)
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.7) +
  # Overlay each subject as a jittered point to show the sample size per group
  geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.2,
                                             dodge.width = 0.75,
                                             seed = 103),
             size = 1.8, alpha = 0.7) +
  # Define colors
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Insufficient (<30 ng/mL)" = "hotpink",
                               "Sufficient (>=30 ng/mL)"  = "skyblue")) +
  # Change labels
  labs(x = "Pregnancy Outcome", y = "*LIN9* Expression", fill = "Vitamin D Status",
       title = "*LIN9* Expression by Pregnancy Outcome\nand Vitamin D Status") +
  # Put the legend on two rows so the full labels fit
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2)) +
  # Set the theme to the custom theme
  Theme

# Print plot
p3

# Save plot as png
ggsave("boxplot_LIN9.png", plot=p3)
```

## Generate a function to produce the submission 1 plots and new plots for the two
additional genes
```{r}
# Function to produce histogram, scatterplot, and boxplot for each gene
buildPlots <- function(data, geneList, contVar, catVars, contLabel = contVar, 
                       catLabels = catVars) {
  # Loop through each gene in the geneList
  for (gene in geneList) {
    # Subset to one current gene
    geneData <- data[data$GENE == gene,]
    
    # Add histogram of gene expression
    plot1 <- ggplot(geneData, aes(x = Expression)) +
      # 15 bins used because it is shows the shape clearly for 157 subjects
      geom_histogram(bins=15, fill= "steelblue", color = "white") +
      # paste0() puts the current gene name into the labels, and *...* italicize
      #the gene name
      labs(x = paste0("*", gene, "* Expression"), y = "Number of Subjects", 
           title = paste0("Distribution of *", gene, "* Expression")) +
      # Apply the custom theme
      Theme
    # Display the plot
    print(plot1)
    
    # Add scatterplot of the continous covariate vs expression
    # x = .data[[contVar]] reads the column whose name is stored in the string, 
    #since x= contVar will plot the text itself
    plot2 <- ggplot(geneData, aes(x = .data[[contVar]], y = Expression)) +
    # alpha=0.7 makes overlapping points visible
      geom_point(color = "steelblue", size = 2, alpha = 0.7) +
      # Avoid a console message by adding formula = y~x
      geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "black", formula = y ~ x) +
      # Set up the axis titles, gene expression
      labs(x = contLabel, y = paste0("*", gene, "* Expression"),
           title = paste0("*", gene, "* Expression vs ", contLabel)) +
      # Apply theme
      Theme
    # Print the second plot 
    print(plot2)
    
    # Add boxplot by both categorical covariates with jittered points
    plot3 <- ggplot(geneData, aes(x = .data[[catVars[1]]], y = Expression,
                               fill = .data[[catVars[2]]])) +
      # Hide the plot's own outliers because all subjects are plotted below and 
      #outliers would be drawn twice otherwise (this was pointed out by Claude when
      #using it to check my function)
      geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.7) +
      # Add jitter (this function is helped by Claude)
      geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.2,
                                                 dodge.width = 0.75,
                                                 # set seed so jitters are the 
                                                 #same each time
                                                 seed = 103),
                 size = 1.8, alpha = 0.7) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = c("hotpink", "skyblue")) +
      labs(x = catLabels[1], y = paste0("*", gene, "* Expression"), fill = catLabels[2],
           title = paste0("*", gene, "* Expression by ", catLabels[1],
                          # break the title into two lines (this function is helped
                          # by Claude)
                          "<br>and ", catLabels[2])) +
      # put legends on two rows so full labels can fit
      guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2)) +
      Theme
    print(plot3)
  }
}
```

## Call the function for each gene
```{r}
# Print the 9 plots using the function
buildPlots(data = df,
           geneList = c("LIN9", "UTS2", "RUNDC3A"),
           contVar = "mat_BMI",
           catVars = c("preg_preeclampsia", "vitD_status"),
           contLabel = "Maternal BMI (kg/m\u00b2)",
           catLabels = c("Pregnancy Outcome", "Vitamin D Status"))
```

## Generate a heat map with a total of 10 genes, 2 categorical variables, and
clustering:

*Chosen genes*: LIN9, UTS2, RUNDC3A, plus the rest 7 genes from the top 10 most 
variable genes, which are TMEM176B, CEACAM6, CLIC2, SLC1A5, ZNF594, ZBTB41, 
CAPZA2. 

Extra resource used: https://jcoliver.github.io/learn-r/009-expression-heatmaps.html


```{r}
# Top 10 most variable genes computed above
head(gene_sd, 10)

# Put the chosen 10 genes into a vector
heatGenes <- c("LIN9", "UTS2", "RUNDC3A", "TMEM176B", "CEACAM6", "CLIC2", "SLC1A5",
               "ZNF594", "ZBTB41", "CAPZA2")

# Use expr_named instead of df because it is already in wide format, which heat map
#needs because it needs one row per gene
heatdf <- expr_named %>%
  # Filter to the 10 genes chosen above. %in% matches any value in the vector
  filter(GENE %in% heatGenes) %>%
  # select the GENE column and all columns whose names start with "GSM", which are 
  #the sample IDs
  select(GENE, starts_with("GSM")) %>%
  # Move the GENE column into the row names so the matrix won't print out text and
  #only holds numbers
  column_to_rownames("GENE") %>%
  # Set it as a matrix so heat map can use it
  as.matrix()
  
# Check the dimension (should be 10 genes and 157 samples)
dim(heatdf)

# Generate a data frame for the tracking bars with one row per sample, and with the
#geoID as row names so pheatmap can match them to the heat map columns
annotationData <- data.frame(row.names = geneData$geoID,
                             "Pregnancy Outcome" = geneData$preg_preeclampsia,
                             "Vitamin D Status" = geneData$vitD_status,
                             # Suggested by Claude, since R's default is check.names
                             #= T, and it replace a space to a dot, so the name would
                             #become pregnancy.outcome
                             check.names = FALSE)

# Define the colors for the tracking bars
annotationColors <- list(
  "Pregnancy Outcome" = c("Normal" = "lightgray", "Preeclampsia" = "purple3"),
  "Vitamin D Status" = c("Insufficient (<30 ng/mL)" = "hotpink",
                         "Sufficient (>=30 ng/mL)" = "skyblue"))

# Generate the heat map with pheatmap function and with clustering
library(pheatmap)

pheatmap(heatdf, 
         # Add cluster
         clustering_distance_rows = "euclidean",
         clustering_distance_cols = "euclidean",
         annotation_col = annotationData,
         annotation_colors = annotationColors,
         #Italicize the gene names: as.expression convert into an expression vector
         #which can be used by a heat map, lapply() applies the function to each 
         #gene, and the rest is the function to build a italic version of the gene name.
         #This function is helped by Claude.
         labels_row = as.expression(lapply(rownames(heatdf),
                                           function(gene) bquote(italic(.(gene))))),
         # Without a scale, the heat map shows raw value; with scale, it shows z-scores
         #(compare a sample to its average in SD units); scale="row" means each gene
         #is compared to itself.
         scale = "row",
         # Remove the 157 samples IDs otherwise they'll all overlap at the bottom
         #(this was generated with help from Claude when checking my heat map)
         show_colnames = FALSE,
         # Save the heat map to a png file using the build-in function in pheatmap
         filename = "gene_heatmap.png")
```
```{r}
# The above pheatmap function will not display the heat map in R after saving it 
#to a png, so display the heat map below again 
knitr::include_graphics("gene_heatmap.png")
```

## Genearte an additional plot type not discussed in class to visualize the gene
data.

I choose to use *Volcano plot* and the EnhancedVolcano package to generate the plot,
since volcano plot is a standard genomics plot, and it uses all 500 genes.

Extra resources are used to generate volcano plot:
https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/EnhancedVolcano/inst/doc
/EnhancedVolcano.html#plot-the-most-basic-volcano-plot 


```{r}
#install.packages("BiocManager")
library(EnhancedVolcano)

# Below is computed with help from Claude, including how to compute t-test
#p-value

# Compute difference in mean expression and t-test p-values (preeclampsia vs normal) 
#in each gene
res <- df %>%
  #group by GENE splits df into 500 groups (one per gene), each with 157 rows
  group_by(GENE) %>%
  summarise(
    # Difference in mean expression between the two pregnancy outcome
    diff = mean(Expression[preg_preeclampsia == "Preeclampsia"]) -
           mean(Expression[preg_preeclampsia == "Normal"]),
    # Welch t-test p-value comparing the two pregnancy outcome
    p = t.test(Expression[preg_preeclampsia == "Preeclampsia"],
               Expression[preg_preeclampsia == "Normal"])$p.value)
  
# Check if there's one row per gene -- it should show 500
nrow(res)

# Convert res into a data frame to be used in the volcano plot
res <- as.data.frame(res)

# Generate the volcano plot
volcano <- EnhancedVolcano(res,
                           #Gene names for the labels
                           lab = res$GENE,
                           #x is the difference in mean expression, y is the p-value
                           x = "diff",
                           y = "p",
                           # Only label the three chosen genes in italics
                           selectLab = c("LIN9", "UTS2", "RUNDC3A"),
                           labFace = "italic",
                           labSize = 5,
                           # Move the labels away if overlap with the point, and 
                           #draw a short line to point to which point it labels
                           drawConnectors = TRUE,
                           # Set up cutoff lines at p=0.05
                           pCutoff = 0.05,
                           # Set up a visual cutoff line at the difference
                           FCcutoff = 0.1,
                           # Set up axis labels
                           xlab = "Difference in mean expression (Preeclampsia - Normal)",
                           # It will plot -log10 by default
                           ylab = "-log10 (unadjusted p-value)",
                           # Rename the legend since the default shows log2 FC
                           legendLabels = c("Neither cutoff", "Difference", "p-value",
                                       "p-value & difference"),
                           # Make legend text smaller so it fits
                           legendLabSize = 10,
                           legendIconSize = 3,
                           # Remove the default title, subtitle, and caption
                           title = NULL,
                           subtitle = NULL,
                           caption = NULL,
                           # Set the limits to zoom in so the points won't be crowded
                           #in the middle
                           xlim = c(-0.4, 0.4),
                           ylim = c(0, 2.5),
                           # Make it looks like the other figures
                           pointSize = 2,
                           gridlines.major = FALSE,
                           gridlines.minor = FALSE
                           )

# Print the plot
volcano 

# Save it to png 
ggsave("volcano_plot.png", plot = volcano)
```

Generate the Summary Statistics table 

```{r}
# Check what type of characters are each variable
str(geneData)
# Convert vitamin D status into factor instead of character
geneData$vitD_status <- factor(geneData$vitD_status,
                               levels = c("Insufficient (<30 ng/mL)",
                                          "Sufficient (>=30 ng/mL)"))
# Check if it is factor now
str(geneData$vitD_status)

# To determine who is a non-normal continuous variable, look at the distribution first
hist(geneData$mat_BMI)
hist(geneData$mat_age_yrs)
hist(geneData$delivery_gestAge_wks)
# All of them look skewed and non-normal. 

# Create a function similar to the function to build table 1
buildTable <- function(data, varList, nonnormVars="", catVars="") {
  # Define an empty table
  table1 <- matrix(nrow = 0, ncol = 2)
  # Keep track of rows to indent
  indentRows <- c()
  # Loop through all variables
  for (var in varList) {
    # Define vector of variable values
    x <- data[,var]
    
    # Identify if a variable is non-normal
    if (var %in% nonnormVars) {
      
      # Calculate medians and IQRs
      myMedian <- round(median(x), 1)
      myIQR1 <- round(quantile(x,1/4),digits = 1)
      myIQR2 <- round(quantile(x,3/4),digits = 1)
      # Combine the values
      value <- paste0(myMedian,' [',myIQR1,', ',myIQR2,']')
      # Define a new row
      newRow <- c(var,value)
      # Add the new row to data
      table1 <- rbind(table1,newRow)
    }
    
    # Identify is a variable is categorical variable
    if (var %in% catVars) {
      
      # Define new row for overall variable
      newRow <- c(var,'')
      # Add row to data frame
      table1 <- rbind(table1,newRow)
      
      # Loop through levels of variable
      for (level in levels(x)) {
        # Calculate n and perc
        n <- sum(x == level)
        perc <- round(n/(length(x)) * 100,digits = 1)
        
        # Combine values
        value <- paste0(n,' (',perc,')')
        
        # Define new row
        newRow <- c(level,value)
        # Add row to data frame
        table1 <- rbind(table1,newRow)
        # Add index to indented rows
        indentRows <- c(indentRows,nrow(table1))
      }
    }
    # Otherwise treat it as normally distributed
    if (!(var %in% c(nonnormVars,catVars))) {
      
      # Calculate the mean and standard deviation
      myMean <- round(mean(x),2)
      mySD <- round(sd(x),2)
      # Combine values
      value <- paste0(myMean,' (',mySD,')')
      
      # Define new row
      newRow <- c(var,value)
      
      # Add row to data frame
      table1 <- rbind(table1,newRow)
    }
  }
  #return the table
  return(table1)
}

# Variables need to be included
vars <- c("mat_BMI", "mat_age_yrs", "delivery_gestAge_wks", "vitD_status")
# From the distribution, all three continuous variables are not normally distributed
nonnorm <- c("mat_BMI", "mat_age_yrs", "delivery_gestAge_wks")

# Create one column for all subjects, one for preeclampsia, and one for normal pregnancy
#outcome
colAll  <- buildTable(geneData, vars, nonnorm, "vitD_status")
colNorm <- buildTable(subset(geneData, preg_preeclampsia == "Normal"),
                         vars, nonnorm, "vitD_status")
colPre   <- buildTable(subset(geneData, preg_preeclampsia == "Preeclampsia"),
                         vars, nonnorm, "vitD_status")

# Put the three columns side by side in the table, and column 1 has the row names
finalTable <- data.frame(colAll[,1], colAll[,2], colNorm[,2], colPre[,2])

# Define the row names 
finalTable[,1] <- c("Maternal BMI (kg/m2), median [IQR]",
                "Maternal age (years), median [IQR]",
                "Gestational age at delivery (weeks), median [IQR]",
                "Vitamin D status, n (%)",
                "Insufficient (<30 ng/mL)",
                "Sufficient (>=30 ng/mL)")

# Define column header names with the sample size (n) of each group (format is helped
#by Claude)
colnames(finalTable) <- c("Variable",
                     paste0("Overall (n = ", nrow(geneData), ")"),
                     paste0("Normal (n = ", sum(geneData$preg_preeclampsia == 
                                                  "Normal"), ")"),
                     paste0("Preeclampsia (n = ", sum(geneData$preg_preeclampsia == 
                                                        "Preeclampsia"), ")"))
# print the final table
finalTable

# Save table as csv file
write.csv(finalTable, "finalTable.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```
